audit_items.proof_trace: The RLS UPDATE policy on `member.members` — `USING (auth.uid() = id/supabase_auth_user_id)` — has no `WITH CHECK` clause and no column-level restriction, allowing any authenticated user to UPDATE any column in their own row, including `is_admin`. The TypeScript generated type (`types.ts:248`) confirms `is_admin?: boolean` is in the `Update` row type. The application-layer admin gate (`admin/layout.tsx:17-21`) only protects Next.js routes; it does not block direct Supabase REST API calls made with the user's own JWT.
audit_items.attack_scenario: An authenticated non-admin user sends `PATCH https://<project>.supabase.co/rest/v1/members?supabase_auth_user_id=eq.<their_uuid>` with their session JWT and body `{"is_admin": true}`; the RLS UPDATE policy permits it because `auth.uid() = supabase_auth_user_id` is satisfied, elevating the attacker to admin and granting full access to all admin routes and data.
